html:
The Achagua are an Arawakan people of the Llanos, the tropical grasslands of eastern Colombia, in Meta and Casanare along the rivers that feed the Orinoco.

Before contact they were farmers and traders whose language was widely used along the rivers. Jesuit missions gathered them into towns in the 1600s and 1700s, and disease and slave raids cut their numbers sharply. Today only a few hundred remain, mostly at the Umapo reserve near Puerto López. Their Arawakan relatives in the region include the Piapoco.
